lesson_title: The Bench That Lies to Your Hand
hook_text: A metal bench and a wooden bench, same cold morning, same temperature. So why does the metal one feel like ice?
clip_script: Put a thermometer on both benches: identical. But touch them, and the metal feels freezing. Here is the trick. Your skin does not sense temperature. It senses how fast you are losing heat. Metal is a conductor: free electrons inside race your heat away from the spot you touch, so your skin keeps cooling. Wood is an insulator: heat barely moves, so the wood under your hand warms up and the flow almost stops. Same reason a tiled floor bites your bare feet but a rug does not. And remember, cold never flows into you. It is always your heat flowing out.
visual_style: Whiteboard split screen of two benches with thermometers showing the same reading, then arrows of heat leaving a hand, many fast arrows into the metal and a few slow ones into the wood.
pacing: Quick setup, a pause for the reveal, a punchy finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn how heat really moves.
